findings.problem: Line 2 says every hiding spot (heavens, Sheol, the farthest sea, the dark) 'gets the same answer: "You are there" (Ps 139:8).' The words 'You are there' appear only for the heavens and Sheol in Psalm 139:8. For the farthest sea the text says 'even there Your hand will guide me' (Psalm 139:9-10), and for the darkness it says 'even the darkness is not dark to You' (Psalm 139:11-12). So it is not the same answer word for word.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match.

findings.problem: Most of the Big Idea walks through the psalm in verse order (lines 2, 3 and 5 especially), repeating what the Prep cards already covered: the hiding spots (Psalm 139:8-12), the knitting and the book of days (Psalm 139:13-16), and the enemies (Psalm 139:20-22). Only lines 1, 6 and 7 say what the psalm means. The stop should summarize what the passage means, not retell it.

rule.text: A real summary of what the passage means, not a retelling of the verses.

findings.problem: 'I used to hide my crooked cookies at the back of the tray' adds a new event to Papa Dorin's backstory. The backstory says his early stamps came out crooked and that he slid to the back of the drawer. It never says he hid crooked cookies on a tray.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Line 1 states as a Bible fact with a reference that God knows 'his naps' (Ps 139:1-12). Psalm 139:3 says 'my lying down', not naps. Line 2 also says 'pitch dark' where Psalm 139:11-12 says only 'darkness'. Both stretch the text in fact lines, not in jokes.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
